newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen rising on back of Dow.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen rising on back of Dow.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to rise at the opening Tuesday on the heels of key U.S. economic data that sent New York markets soaring.

But traders said while U.S. long bond yields dived to 7.01 percent from 7.12 percent on a much lower expected rise in the Employment Cost Index (ECI), several more crucial economic indicators were due out this week.

"We've got to take it one day at a time," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "Round one has been won by the markets, but there's several more rounds to be fought before we can claim victory this week over economic data."
U.S. gross domestic product figures and management purchasing data are due out Wednesday while the all-important payrolls report comes in Friday.

"If there are several more very good numbers, then the long bond yield may finally turn around and settle below seven percent, which would give stock markets a real lift," Bonanno said. "Otherwise the trend will be negative, with yields aiming for 7.25 percent and slumping bourses."
Traders also said this week's slim trading volumes, both at home and abroad, made the markets especially vulnerable to sharp swings.

"Yesterday here we didn't even make it to 10 million pesos -- that's pathetic and means anybody can take us by storm," another trader said, noting local private pension funds "are nowhere to be seen."
The blue-chip MerVal .MERV index inched up 0.1 percent Monday to 716.51 and floor volume dwindled to 9.7 million pesos, or about a third of the amount considered a healthy turnover.
The MerVal still stands 1.5 percent higher so far in April.
